title: Semi Dull vs Bright vs Full Dull Polyester Yarn: What's the Difference?
excerpt: Choosing the right luster for your yarn is critical to the final look and feel of your fabric. In this guide, we break down the three main luster types available in polyester yarn.
body:
When sourcing polyester yarn — whether POY, FDY, or DTY — one of the most important specifications is luster. Luster refers to the optical brightness of the yarn, which directly impacts how the finished fabric looks and feels.

Semi Dull (SD)

Semi Dull yarn contains a small amount of TiO₂ (titanium dioxide) to reduce shine. It produces a natural, matte-like appearance that closely resembles cotton. It's the most commonly used variant in everyday apparel, home textiles, and industrial applications. SD yarn is ideal when you want a clean, professional finish without excessive sheen.

Bright (FD Bright / Super Bright)

Bright polyester has no TiO₂ added, giving it a high-gloss, lustrous appearance. This makes it perfect for decorative fabrics, sari borders, sportswear linings, and any application that benefits from extra visual appeal. However, Bright yarn can highlight imperfections in weaving more readily than SD.

Full Dull (FD)

Full Dull yarn contains a higher concentration of TiO₂, giving it the most muted, non-reflective appearance of the three. It closely mimics natural fibers like wool and cotton, and is heavily used in premium fashion garments, technical textiles, and sustainable fashion where the goal is a natural hand feel.

Which Should You Choose?

The right choice depends on your end application:
• Everyday apparel / home textiles → Semi Dull
• Decorative / evening wear / sportswear → Bright
• Premium fashion / natural-look fabrics → Full Dull

title: Why Surat is India's Undisputed Textile Capital
excerpt: From humble beginnings as a silk trading port, Surat today produces over 40% of India's synthetic fabric output. We explore why this city continues to lead India's textile industry.
body:
Located on the banks of the Tapi River in Gujarat, Surat is often called the "Diamond City" of India — but its textile industry rivals its diamond trade in global significance.

A Rich History

Surat's textile trade dates back to the Mughal era when the city was a major port for silk and cotton exports. With the industrial revolution and the advent of power looms in the 20th century, Surat rapidly pivoted to synthetic fabrics — polyester, nylon, and viscose — becoming a dominant textile hub.

Scale of Operations

Today, Surat accounts for:
• 40%+ of India's synthetic fabric production
• Over 4,00,000 power looms
• A thriving network of weaving, dyeing, printing, and embroidery units
• A major hub for yarn trading — both domestic and imported

The Reshamwala Market

At the heart of Surat's yarn trade is the iconic Reshamwala Market on Ring Road — where Surat Sales Private Limited has operated since 2009. This market is where traders, weavers, and manufacturers converge to source yarn, fabrics, and raw materials at competitive prices.

Why It Matters for Your Sourcing

Being based in Surat gives Surat Sales a strategic advantage. We have direct relationships with local manufacturers and national distributors, giving you access to the widest selection of yarn types, lusters, and deniers — at prices that reflect our buying power and market knowledge.

title: POY vs FDY vs DTY: Which Yarn is Right for Your Application?
excerpt: Confused about whether you need POY, FDY, or DTY? This practical guide explains what each yarn type is, how it's made, and which textile applications each is best suited for.
body:
Polyester yarn comes in several forms depending on how far along the manufacturing process it has gone. Understanding the difference is key to choosing the right raw material for your application.

POY — Partially Oriented Yarn

What is it? A semi-finished polyester yarn produced by melt-spinning polyester chips (PET) at high speed. It's "partially" oriented — meaning the molecular chains are not fully aligned.

Used for: Primarily as feed yarn for further processing into DTY (via texturizing) or FDY (via drawing). Not suitable for direct weaving.

Key specs: 75D–600D, Semi Dull / Bright / Full Dull

FDY — Fully Drawn Yarn

What is it? Produced by fully drawing and orienting the polyester during spinning in a single continuous process. FDY is a finished yarn — smooth, flat, and ready to weave.

Used for: Warp knitting, weaving, fabrics requiring a smooth, flat texture — chiffon, georgette, lining fabrics, satin.

Key specs: 20D–1000D, all luster types

DTY — Draw Textured Yarn

What is it? Produced by texturizing POY through a false-twist texturing process, giving the yarn a crimped, bulky, soft texture similar to natural fibers.

Used for: Knitting, hosiery, casual wear, sportswear, stretch fabrics. DTY is soft to touch and has good elasticity.

Key specs: 50D–600D, all luster types, multiple twist directions (S/Z)

Quick Reference

• Smooth, flat fabric (satin, chiffon, georgette) → FDY
• Soft, textured fabric (jersey, fleece, sportswear) → DTY
• Input for your own texturizing machine → POY

title: The Rise of Recycled PET: How rPET is Reshaping the Textile Industry
excerpt: Recycled PET (rPET) — made from post-consumer plastic bottles — is rapidly becoming mainstream in textile manufacturing. What does this mean for yarn buyers and mills in India?
body:
The textile industry is one of the world's largest polluters, and the shift toward sustainable raw materials is no longer optional — it's becoming a market requirement. At the center of this shift is rPET (Recycled Polyethylene Terephthalate) yarn, sometimes called GRS-certified recycled yarn.

What is rPET Yarn?

rPET yarn is spun from recycled PET flakes, which are derived from post-consumer polyester — primarily single-use plastic bottles (PET bottles). The bottles are cleaned, shredded into flakes, melted, and re-spun into yarn using conventional polyester spinning equipment.

Why is it Growing?

• Brand demand — Global brands like H&M, Zara, Adidas, Nike have committed to using X% recycled content in their supply chains by 2030
• Comparable performance — rPET yarn has similar tensile strength, dye fastness, and processability to virgin polyester
• Carbon footprint — rPET production generates ~30–50% fewer CO₂ emissions than virgin polyester
• Regulatory pressure — EU and US import regulations increasingly ask for sustainability documentation

Challenges in the Indian Market

While rPET adoption is growing, Indian mills face challenges:
• Higher raw material cost (rPET is ~10–20% more expensive than virgin PET chips)
• Certification requirements (GRS certification adds administrative overhead)
• Inconsistent quality from smaller recyclers

What This Means for You

At Surat Sales, we are watching the rPET market closely and working with our supply chain partners to be ready to offer certified rPET yarn when demand from Indian mills reaches critical mass. If you are currently being asked by buyers to shift to recycled content, contact us — we can help you navigate the options.
